name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa
summary: The Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa is a 10-year visa run by Thailand's Board of Investment (BOI) for well-off and highly skilled foreigners. There are four categories: Wealthy Global Citizens, Wealthy Pensioners, Work-from-Thailand Professionals and Highly Skilled Professionals. Holders get a 5-year stay renewable for another 5, a yearly address report instead of every 90 days, and, depending on the category, a digital work permit and a 17% flat income tax rate.
seoTitle: Thailand LTR Visa 2026: 10-Year Visa Requirements and Benefits
seoDescription: The Thai Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa explained: four categories, income and asset thresholds, health insurance, 50,000 THB fee, digital work permit and the 17% tax rate.
validity: 10 years, multiple entry. You're first given 5 years of stay, which is extended for another 5 years if you still meet the criteria.
extendableDetail: After the first 5 years you apply to renew for the second 5 years. You must still meet your category's conditions (income, assets, investment, job and insurance). You can also switch category, for example from Highly Skilled Professional to Wealthy Pensioner, if you qualify.
feeNote: The BOI lists a processing fee of 50,000 THB per person for the 10-year multiple-entry visa when you collect it in Thailand. At a Thai embassy abroad the fee is charged in local currency and may differ.
financialRequirement: Depends on your category. Wealthy Global Citizens: at least USD 1 million in assets, including USD 500,000 invested in Thailand. Wealthy Pensioners (50+): USD 80,000 a year in pension or passive income, or USD 40,000 plus USD 250,000 invested in Thailand. Work-from-Thailand and Highly Skilled Professionals: USD 80,000 a year average income over the past two years, or USD 40,000 with a master's degree or higher. Everyone also needs health insurance of USD 50,000 (or Thai social security, or USD 100,000 in the bank for 12 months).
processingTime: The BOI takes about 3 working days for a preliminary check and then about 17 working days for the government agency review, longer if they ask for more documents. After endorsement you have 60 days to collect the visa. The digital work permit, if you need one, takes 3 to 5 working days.
keyRequirements: Qualify for one of the four categories (wealth, pension, remote work for a large employer, or a skilled job in a targeted industry)
Health insurance with at least USD 50,000 cover, Thai social security, or USD 100,000 held in the bank for at least 12 months
Wealthy Pensioners must be 50 or older
Work-from-Thailand: your employer must be listed on a stock exchange or have at least USD 50 million revenue over the last three years and 3 years in operation
Highly Skilled Professionals: work for a business, university or government agency in a BOI targeted industry
Keep meeting all conditions for the whole time you hold the visa
documents: Health insurance certificate (USD 50,000 cover) or proof of Thai social security or USD 100,000 deposit
Tax returns or payslips showing your income for the past two years (income-based categories)
Statements of pension, dividends, rent or other passive income (Wealthy Pensioners)
Proof of at least USD 1 million in assets and USD 500,000 invested in Thailand (Wealthy Global Citizens)
Employment contract and employer's company documents (Work-from-Thailand and Highly Skilled Professionals)
Degree certificate if you rely on the USD 40,000 threshold with a master's degree
Marriage or birth certificates for dependants
Criminal record check if requested by the BOI or embassy

howToApply.detail: Read the category criteria on ltr.boi.go.th. Pick one category only. Each has its own document checklist to download.

howToApply.step: Apply online to the BOI for endorsement
howToApply.detail: Create an account at visa.boi.go.th and upload your documents. The BOI does a preliminary check (about 3 working days) and sends the file to the relevant agencies (about 17 working days).
The endorsement letter is valid for 60 days. Within that time you must collect your visa, or you'll need to apply again.

howToApply.step: Get the visa in Thailand or abroad
howToApply.detail: Collect it at the BOI's One Stop Service Center in Bangkok (fee 50,000 THB) or at a Thai embassy or consulate abroad. Bring the documents the immigration pre-approval asks for.

howToApply.step: Apply for the digital work permit if you need one
howToApply.detail: Highly Skilled Professionals receive a digital work permit. Wealthy Global Citizens, Wealthy Pensioners and dependants can request one. Work-from-Thailand holders work for a foreign employer and don't receive one.

howToApply.step: Report yearly and keep conditions up
howToApply.detail: Instead of 90-day reports you report your address once a year. Keep your insurance, income, investment and job valid, because the BOI can check them.

bestFor: Remote employees of large, established foreign companies
Highly skilled professionals hired by a Thai company or institution in a targeted industry
Retirees over 50 with a substantial pension or passive income
Wealthy individuals willing to invest USD 500,000 in Thailand
Families who want a long, stable visa with dependants included
notFor: Freelancers or employees of small companies (look at the DTV)
Retirees with a smaller pension (look at the Non-O or Non-O-A retirement visas)
Startup founders (the SMART S visa is aimed at you)
Anyone who can't show the income for the full period required
commonMistakes: Applying under Work-from-Thailand when your employer doesn't meet the listed-company or USD 50 million revenue test.
Using salary to qualify as a Wealthy Pensioner. Only pension and passive income such as dividends, rent or interest counts.
Letting health insurance lapse, or buying a policy with less than USD 50,000 cover.
Missing the 60-day window to collect the visa after BOI endorsement.
Assuming the 17% tax rate applies to every holder. It applies to Highly Skilled Professionals' Thai employment income.

faqs.q: How long is the LTR visa valid?
faqs.a: 10 years in total. You're first given 5 years, then extended for another 5 years if you still meet the conditions.

faqs.q: Does the LTR come with a work permit?
faqs.a: Highly Skilled Professionals get a digital work permit. Wealthy Global Citizens, Wealthy Pensioners and dependants can ask for one. Work-from-Thailand Professionals work remotely for a foreign employer and aren't given a Thai work permit. LTR holders are also exempt from the rule that an employer needs 4 Thai staff per foreigner.

faqs.q: Do I pay only 17% income tax?
faqs.a: The 17% flat personal income tax rate is for Highly Skilled Professionals on income from their Thai employment. The BOI also lists a tax exemption for overseas income for LTR holders. Tax rules are complex, so speak to a Thai tax adviser before you rely on either benefit.

faqs.q: What is the minimum income for the LTR?
faqs.a: USD 80,000 a year on average over the past two years for Work-from-Thailand and Highly Skilled Professionals, or USD 40,000 if you hold a master's degree or higher. Wealthy Pensioners need USD 80,000 a year of passive income, or USD 40,000 plus USD 250,000 invested in Thailand. Wealthy Global Citizens have no income test after the 2025 changes, only asset and investment tests.

Yes. Your spouse and children under 20 can get LTR dependant visas. Each dependant needs USD 25,000 of health insurance (or equivalent). The BOI website states a maximum of 4 dependants; a 2025 Cabinet decision was reported to widen this, so check the latest rules.

faqs.q: Do I still need to do 90-day reports?
faqs.a: No. LTR holders report their address once a year instead of every 90 days, and they don't need a separate re-entry permit when they travel.

faqs.q: Can a freelancer or small-business owner get the LTR?
faqs.a: Usually not through Work-from-Thailand: your employer must be a listed company or have at least USD 50 million revenue over three years. Freelancers and small-company employees usually look at the DTV instead.
